title: Lower-left anchored rectangle packing constant
formal: Determine the universal lower-left anchored rectangle packing constant \(\alpha\) to absolute error at most \(1/100\). For each finite point set \(P\subseteq[0,1)^2\) containing \((0,0)\), let \(A(P)\) be the supremum of the total area of all valid packings of one positive-area axis-aligned rectangle per point, each anchored at that point as its lower-left corner and contained in the unit square. Rectangles must have disjoint interiors. Define \(\alpha=\inf_{P\subseteq[0,1)^2,\;P\text{ finite},\;(0,0)\in P}A(P)\). Area is measured as a fraction of the unit square, so the tolerance is one percentage point of its area.
why: The question asks how much area arbitrary anchors inevitably permit one to occupy. Its mathematical interest comes from the universal guarantee over every finite configuration, including degeneracies, rather than the optimal value of one instance. The half-area conjecture would identify the extremal value, while rigorous estimates of the constant quantify the remaining gap.
status_note: The checked 2021 primary paper and 2023 dissertation leave Freedman’s exact conjecture open and give the interval 0.39 to 0.5 for the associated universal coverage constant. The 2013 proof announcement was explicitly withdrawn. Bounded later-work checks through 2026-09-15 found no verified resolution at the stated precision; this is not an exhaustive certification of all subsequent literature.

progress.text: Freedman poses the half-coverage question, as documented in the checked 2021 paper’s introduction and its reference to Tutte’s collection of unsolved problems.
The authors withdraw the announced existential proof because of an error in Claim 5.

Damerius, Kaaser, Kling and Schneider publish a 39 percent coverage guarantee and a below-43.3-percent limitation for their studied greedy algorithm. The half-coverage conjecture remains a separate general question.
Nölke’s dissertation, defended on 21 February 2023, retains the open conjecture and the 0.39 universal guarantee in its introduction and Chapter 3.

importance.reason: A longstanding geometric extremal problem whose elementary input model hides a large unresolved gap between universal coverage guarantees. It links continuous packing choices with arbitrary finite point configurations, and the demonstrated limitation of the familiar greedy algorithm separates general existence from that algorithm’s performance.

sentences: The target is the worst possible optimal coverage by rectangles anchored at their lower-left corners at arbitrary points of the unit square.
Every finite point set must include the origin, and each point receives a positive-area rectangle with no interior overlap.
The numerical answer must locate the universal coverage constant within one percentage point, with a complete Lean proof.
Freedman’s exact half-coverage conjecture remains the source question and is stronger than satisfying this approximation criterion.
The checked universal bounds are 39 and 50 percent, while the smaller upper bound in the 2021 paper concerns only its particular greedy algorithm.

definitions: Write \(p=(x_p,y_p)\). A valid packing chooses real coordinates \(u_p,v_p\) satisfying \(x_p<u_p\le1\) and \(y_p<v_p\le1\) for every \(p\in P\), and uses \(R_p=[x_p,u_p)\times[y_p,v_p)\). For distinct points \(p,q\), the open sets \((x_p,u_p)\times(y_p,v_p)\) and \((x_q,u_q)\times(y_q,v_q)\) must be disjoint; boundaries may touch. Its total area is \(\sum_{p\in P}(u_p-x_p)(v_p-y_p)\). All points are distinct, their number is arbitrary, and coordinates may be any real numbers in the stated domain. Points may share an x-coordinate or y-coordinate; there is no general-position assumption. The origin is mandatory. The other three corners of a rectangle need not belong to \(P\). Every point anchors exactly one positive-area rectangle, and no rotations, other anchor corners, squares-only restriction, or overlaps of positive area are permitted. Valid packings exist for every such finite set, and their areas are bounded by one. Thus \(A(P)\) and \(\alpha\) are well-defined real suprema and infima. No optimum-attaining point set or packing is demanded by the definitions. There is no computational running-time requirement and no rational-coordinate or finite-precision restriction.
answer_criterion: Supply an unambiguous real value \(a\) and a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean that \(|a-\alpha|\le1/100\), with the quantifiers, positivity and boundary conventions above. Equivalently, certify an interval \([L,U]\) containing \(\alpha\) with \(U-L\le1/50\) and take its midpoint. A lower bound \(L\) must hold for every finite allowed point set through its packing supremum; an upper bound \(U\) must bound the infimum over all allowed point sets, allowing a sequence of sets approaching the bound. A value of \(A(P)\) for one selected instance, an uncertified experiment, or only a performance guarantee for a particular algorithm is insufficient. Exact determination is welcome but not required. This numerical benchmark does not claim that a one-percentage-point approximation proves or refutes the exact half-coverage conjecture.

context_blocks.text: Freedman’s original conjecture asks whether every permitted point set admits a packing covering at least \(1/2\) of the square. The ICALP 2021 source states this in its introduction and calls for algorithms reaching that guarantee in its conclusion. This card follows the authorized numerical formulation of extremal targets: it asks for the underlying universal coverage constant, retaining the exact conjecture here as the source question. The numerical acceptance criterion is a broadening, not a claim of logical equivalence to proving the conjecture.

The checked 2021 paper establishes a universal coverage guarantee of \(0.39\), while its introductory extremal comparison gives \(\alpha\le1/2\). Consequently the checked bounds are \(0.39\le\alpha\le0.5\). This interval is wider than the benchmark’s permitted \(1/50\) certified interval.

The same paper exhibits inputs on which its studied greedy packing algorithm covers less than \(0.433\). That is an upper bound on this particular algorithm’s worst-case guarantee. It is not an upper bound of \(0.433\) on the optimum packing constant \(\alpha\), and it does not refute Freedman’s conjecture.

A 2013 preprint announcing a proof was withdrawn on 28 April 2014 because its authors found a bug in Claim 5. Its unchanged abstract must be read together with the withdrawal notice; it is not a verified resolution.

Nölke’s 2023 dissertation still records the half-coverage conjecture as open and cites 0.39 as the best known universal guarantee. Its other anchored-packing variants have different allowed anchor positions and do not automatically settle the lower-left problem.
